citations.assessment: The corresponding Zunin notice explicitly gives Heilprin’s two-namesake inference. The Hebrew parenthesis signals an internal cross-reference.
The base reads Boethus ben Zonen and explicitly attributes the field arrangement to Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah. The parties dispute who ate the produce.
The parallel names Boethus ben Zonin and retains the disagreement over who ate the produce.
The Mishnah discusses the loan with a field as security and the condition after three years. It names the sages collectively.
The subject here is whether his eight prophetic books were joined in one volume. Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah is named, and another reading says each book was separate.
The stated discussion concerns decorated unleavened cakes and takes place before Rabban Gamliel and the sages in Yavneh.

evidence.witness: The Jerusalem Talmud, edition by Heinrich W. Guggenheimer. Berlin, De Gruyter, 1999-2015

citations.assessment: Rabban Gamliel and the elders reclined in Boethus ben Zonin’s house in Lod.
Rav Yehudah transmits that Boethus asked the sages about decorated unleavened cakes.
Rav Yehudah reports Boethus ben Zonin reciting before Rabbi in the discussion of weighing.
